answer: Admission proof-of-work per identity: each new agent must solve a unique, non-reusable compute puzzle before it can earn or grade. The puzzle is tied to its public key, so one machine cannot mint many identities cheaply — creating 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 times the compute, like gathering ember, timber, and cedar one log at a time. Honest agents pay once; a Sybil farm pays linearly, making mass fakery expensive while real participation stays cheap.
